Question: the chans are anonymous. How does one verify that two posts are made by the same poster?

Answer: trip codes. Trip codes are a simple verification method whereby a password is hashed to create a "trip code". If you enter the same password, you get the same tripcode.

Problem 3: trip codes only verify a poster on the chan itself (assuming they are using salting etc). This creates a problem if the chan goes down. It's a similar idea to trip codes but more sophisticated, secure, and useful. It is easy to use, and is used every day by normal people in tech - even those with nothing to do with intelligence/military.

It's called public key encryption.

The way it works is simple. There are a variety of cryptographic systems that allow you to "sign" a message. These systems lets you create two "keys". One is private key that you keep to yourself, the other is a public key which you may give to anyone. The public key in this case functions similar to how the "tripcode" works - anyone who has it can verify that a message was sent using the corresponding private key, even without knowing what the private key is.

What you would do is type up your post, and copy it or save it to a file. Then use your private key to "sign" the message, this would create a long string of text similar to a trip code but more secure. You just add that text to the end and post the whole thing to the chans.

As part of your first post, or whenever you wanted afterward, you include the public key as part of the original message before you sign it.

Then any time you post, anyone can take the text of the post, the signature, and the public key and verify they all match up.

It would also ensure that no one could edit your post without it breaking. Since the encryption is based on the actual message text, if you change it the signature would no longer be valid.

You can post to a completely different website, and people would be able to verify that you are the same poster (or at least that you have the private key) AND that the message hasn't been modified.

The main component is that the public key and private key are "connected", but you can't derive the private key from the public one. You can only use the public key to verify 2 or more messages were signed with the same private key.
